headline: Pivotal cancer trial succeeds as R&D spend accelerates
summary_short: Revolution Medicines widened its net loss to $453.8M in Q1 FY2026 (from $364.9M q/q and $213.4M y/y) as R&D spend rose 67% to fund four Phase 3 RAS(ON) inhibitor trials, while its lead program, daraxonrasib, went on to report a statistically significant survival benefit in pancreatic cancer shortly after quarter-end.
summary_long: R&D expenses rose 67% ($138.2M) on higher clinical and manufacturing costs for daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib, added headcount, and stock-based compensation tied to a retirement-benefit plan change; G&A rose 189% ($66.2M) on similar comp and commercial-preparation costs. Net loss widened to $453.8M from $364.9M q/q and $213.4M y/y. Operating cash burn was $354.2M, up from $194.4M a year ago. The company held $440.9M in cash and equivalents ($1.9B including marketable securities) at quarter-end after raising $226.7M via its ATM program in the quarter. Subsequent to quarter-end, RASolute 302 met its primary survival endpoints and the company raised $2.1B in follow-on equity plus $500M via convertible notes. Management gives no formal revenue or EPS guidance; the company remains pre-commercial.

drivers.explanation: Losses widened as R&D and G&A both accelerated to fund four Phase 3 registrational trials ahead of a planned first NDA filing; daraxonrasib's RASolute 302 trial met its primary survival endpoints in April 2026.
R&D rose $138.2M (67%) on higher daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib clinical/manufacturing spend, headcount and stock-based comp; G&A rose $66.2M (189%) on similar comp and commercial-prep costs.
Driven by the same R&D and G&A increases disclosed in the release, with zero revenue to offset the higher spending.
Tracks the operating-loss widening one-for-one; no revenue exists yet to offset increased R&D/G&A spend on late-stage trials.
Net loss widened while diluted shares outstanding grew about 5% y/y on ATM equity sales, both pushing EPS further negative.
Cash used in operations was primarily attributable to the $453.8M net loss, partly offset by $87.3M of non-cash stock-based compensation.
Cash and equivalents rose q/q as the company sold $226.7M of common stock under its ATM programs during the quarter, outpacing operating cash burn.
Equity declined as the quarter's net loss outpaced new equity raised via ATM sales and stock-based compensation.
Revolution Medicines remains pre-commercial with no approved products; zero revenue is a structural fact for a clinical-stage biotech, not a miss.
